newsitem.title: USA: Dana says buys off-highway parts maker.
newsitem.headline: Dana says buys off-highway parts maker.

text.p: Dana Corp said Friday it agreed to acquire Clark-Hurth Components, a maker of off-highway vehicle parts, from Ingersoll-Rand Co.
Dana said terms were not disclosed but said the acquisition is the largest in Dana's 92-year history.
Clark-Hurth's 1995 sales were about $350 million, Dana said in a statement. The acquisition is contingent on customary conditions including regulatory approval, Dana said.
"This acquisition will make Dana a leading supplier of off-highway drivetrain components and systems," Dana chairman Southwood Morcott said in the statement.

It will also strengthen Dana's international presence because two-thirds of Clark-Hurth sales are outside the U.S., he said. "It will bring together broad manufacturing experience, superior engineering expertise and global delivery capabilities," he said.

Dana said it will combine Clark-Hurth operations with Dana's Spicer off-highway divisions, forming an off-highway components group that will make axles, brakes, transaxles and powershift transmissions and modular systems for agriculture, construction, forestry, leisure and outdoor power equipment.

Clark-Hurth has manufacturing facilities in Belgium, Italy and the U.S., and more than half of its sales are in Europe, Dana said. Spicer has plants in the U.S., United Kingdom and Italy. Dana said the acquisition better positions it for Asian and South American markets as well.
